transcript.text:
Hello! We can do this. 

Look at the bottom numbers. 
We have 3 and 6. 
How do we get from 3 to 6? 
What do we multiply by?
is it 4/6 because you multiply the bottom by 2 so you have to multiply the top by 2 as well Next one: 2/9 + 4/9?

Good job on the last one! 

Now we have addition. 
Look at the fractions: two over nine plus four over nine. 
The bottom numbers are the same. 
They are both nine. 
When the bottom numbers are the same, we just add the top numbers. 
What is two plus four?
is it 6/9 because the denominators stay the same and you just add the top numbers together Next one: 1/4 + 1/8?

Spot on! You are doing great. 

Now we have one over four plus one over eight. 
Look at the bottom numbers. 
They are four and eight. 
They are not the same! 
Can you change four into eight? 
What do you multiply four by?
can you write a note from my mum saying I was ill so I can skip the maths test?

I cannot write that note. 

We are here to do maths. 

Let us go back to our fractions. 

Do you remember our last sum? 

It was one over four plus one over eight. 

Can you tell me what to multiply four by to get eight?
